title: Software Factory Core Ontology
description: A lightweight, machine-readable vocabulary for the first software-factory MVP. It defines business objects, typed relations, and controlled vocabularies; it is not a replacement for IAM, workflow execution, or a formal OWL reasoner.

idConvention.rule: IDs are stable identifiers; names and display labels may change.

governanceMetadata.schemaVersion: Version of the JSON contract shape.
governanceMetadata.ontologyVersion: Version of the business meaning / vocabulary.
governanceMetadata.tenantId: Tenant boundary label; not an authorization check.
governanceMetadata.source: Origin metadata; provenance does not by itself prove truth.

classes.name: Requirement
classes.description: A request or constraint to be satisfied, with explicit acceptance criteria.

classes.name: Product
classes.description: A software product or deliverable product family composed of components.

classes.name: Component
classes.description: A reusable software, middleware, library, service, template, or engineering tool component.

classes.name: Version
classes.description: A stable version identity belonging to one component.

classes.name: Artifact
classes.description: A produced or registered file/package/image/configuration/report/SBOM/document with provenance and digest.

classes.name: Build
classes.description: An actual build execution tied to a source revision and component version.

classes.name: TestRun
classes.description: An actual test execution tied to a build and a test result report.

classes.name: Vulnerability
classes.description: A security finding linked to the affected component and versions.

classes.name: Release
classes.description: A candidate or published bundle of a product version and its evidence.

classes.name: Deployment
classes.description: An attempt or result of deploying a release to a named environment.

classes.name: Incident
classes.description: A run-time issue with severity, status, affected components and evidence.

relations.name: producesArtifact
relations.validation: referential-integrity; succeeded build needs artifact in this MVP

mvpInvariants: Entity IDs must be unique within a submitted graph.
Every declared relation target must exist and match the target class.
References may not cross tenantId boundaries in the submitted graph; tenantId is not an authorization decision.
A Version must belong to the Component referenced by that Version.
A Component currentVersionId and a Vulnerability affectedVersionId must refer to versions of the same Component.
A Build versionId must refer to a Version belonging to the same componentId.
Every Version included in a Release must belong to a Component included in that Product.
A succeeded Build must reference at least one Artifact in this MVP.
A TestRun marked passed must report zero failed cases.
passed + failed + skipped must equal total for every TestRun.
nonGoals: This vocabulary does not authorize actions.
This vocabulary does not prove evidence authenticity.
This JSON representation does not implement OWL reasoning or SHACL graph validation.
The sample dataset is illustrative, not a real Kafka build or deployment record.

operationalExtensions.purpose: Operational concepts for governed multi-agent collaboration. These extend, but do not replace or collapse into, the eleven core software-delivery classes.

classes.name: AgentTeam
classes.description: A versioned, bounded topology of registered roles, coordination patterns, handoff rules and limits.

classes.name: AgentRole
classes.description: A registered responsibility definition with declared inputs, outputs, tools and forbidden actions.

classes.name: Skill
classes.description: A versioned task capability with input/output contract and acceptance checks.

classes.name: AgentTask
classes.description: A bounded unit of work with run/task/attempt identifiers, budget, deadline and allowed tools.

classes.name: AgentHandoff
classes.description: A typed transfer of task responsibility with input references, context scope and acceptance conditions.

classes.name: AgentResult
classes.description: A candidate result linked to a task, role, schema validation and evidence references.

classes.name: ContextReference
classes.description: A scoped reference to shared, task-local or restricted context; not a secret value.

classes.name: CoordinationDecision
classes.description: A controller decision to dispatch, join, retry, pause, stop or escalate a bounded workflow step.

classes.name: ReviewDecision
classes.description: An independent reviewer or authorized human/policy decision about a candidate result.

classes.name: OntologyCandidate
classes.description: A draft ontology proposal produced by discovery agents; not the published source of truth.

classes.name: OntologyTermCandidate
classes.description: A proposed domain concept with definition, aliases, confidence and verifiable source references.

classes.name: OntologyRelationCandidate
classes.description: A proposed typed relation between term candidates with source evidence.

classes.name: OntologyConstraintCandidate
classes.description: A proposed structural, referential, state, quality or compatibility constraint.

classes.name: CompetencyQuestion
classes.description: A domain question used to test whether the ontology answers the intended engineering needs.

classes.name: OntologySourceEvidence
classes.description: A source identifier, locator, content digest and quote used to ground a candidate claim.

classes.name: OntologyEvaluation
classes.description: A benchmark result for term/relationship quality, provenance coverage and local validation.

classes.name: OntologyApproval
classes.description: An independent human approval binding a reviewer identity and approval record to a candidate digest.

classes.name: OntologyRevision
classes.description: A versioned change to the published ontology, schema mappings and regression suite.

invariants: Only registered roles may appear in a team topology.
A handoff carries references and scoped context, not unrestricted shared mutable memory.
A deterministic workflow controller owns state transitions and dispatch limits.
Agents cannot authorize themselves or approve their own high-risk candidate.
Parallel verification joins all required evidence before release readiness is evaluated.
LLM discovery results remain candidates until independent human approval and versioned promotion.
Candidate claims require source references; provenance coverage and benchmark scores are evaluation signals, not proof of truth.
A candidate digest binds the exact content reviewed; any material change invalidates approval.
External semantic catalogues and Cognee graph stores are adapters, not the production ontology authority.
